background.task: The experience subsystem evaluation was **partially successful**. The core **save** and **deep-learn** operations work correctly — traces are persisted to disk and deep learning analysis produces verified/hypothesis facts. However, **experience list** and **experience query** both return empty results (0 entries / P5 cold start) until `experience deep-learn` has been run on a given domain+intent. This means `experience save` alone is insufficient to make knowledge queryable — a critical gap not documented anywhere. Additionally, several response fields are missing or incorrect (failure_category, task_type, intent auto-classification), filtering has bugs (intent-filter leaks, page-size ignored), and URL validation is absent.

issues.title: experience list/query return empty until deep-learn is run — save does not index knowledge

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. Run `experience save` for a new domain+intent (returns saved=true).
2. Run `experience list` or `experience query` for that domain — returns 0 entries / P5 cold start.
3. Run `experience deep-learn --force` for that domain+intent.
4. Run `experience list` or `experience query` again — now returns results.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: experience save should make knowledge immediately queryable via list and query. The documentation implies save stores the trace and updates stats — list/query should find it without requiring deep-learn.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: experience list returns 0 entries and experience query returns P5 cold start until deep-learn is explicitly run for each domain+intent pair. Traces saved via save() and experience YAML files exist on disk but are not indexed for retrieval until deep_learn triggers indexing.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The KnowledgeStore's list() and query() methods read from an in-memory index or a different data structure than the raw trace/experience files on disk. deep_learn() triggers a rebuild/scan of the knowledge directory that populates this index. save() writes files but does not update the retrieval index. The code paths are disconnected: save writes to the filesystem store; list/query read from an index that is only populated by deep_learn.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Have experience save() call the same index-rebuild logic that deep_learn() triggers, so saved knowledge is immediately queryable
- Alternatively, have list() and query() scan the experience/ directory directly instead of relying on a separate index
- Add a background index refresh or file watcher so new traces are automatically indexed
- Document the current behavior as a known limitation if the index rebuild is intentionally deferred to deep_learn

issues.title: failure_category is always 'unknown' — error message classification not working

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run: `./b4w.ps1 experience save "https://blocked.example.com/search" '{"url":"...","errorMessage":"CAPTCHA detected on page",...}' --outcome failure --intent "search for product"`

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: failure_category should be "anti_bot" (classified from the CAPTCHA error message) or "timeout" (from timeout messages).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: failure_category is always "unknown" regardless of the error message content. Tested with "CAPTCHA detected on page" and "Timeout waiting for selector" — both produced "unknown".

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The failure classification logic either does not exist, is not invoked, or its pattern-matching rules don't cover the error messages being tested. The errorMessage field from the trace is stored but not parsed for categorization.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Implement pattern-matching on the errorMessage field to classify failures into anti_bot, timeout, selector_not_found, network_error, etc.
- Add a --failure-category option to allow users to explicitly set the category
- If classification is intentionally deferred, document that failure_category will be 'unknown' unless explicitly provided

issues.title: Auto-classified intent is 'other' instead of matching taskType when --intent is omitted

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run: `./b4w.ps1 experience save "https://example.com/login" '{"url":"...","taskType":"login",...}'` (no --intent flag).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Intent should be auto-classified as "login" based on the trace's taskType field.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Intent is classified as "other". The taskType field in the trace JSON is not used for intent classification.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The auto-classification logic does not read the taskType field from the trace JSON. It may only use a default fallback value ('other') when no --intent is provided.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Read the taskType field from the trace JSON and map it to the corresponding intent (login→LOGIN, extract_product_detail→EXTRACT, search→SEARCH, fill_form→FILL_FORM, etc.)
- Add a taskType-to-intent mapping table as a fallback when --intent is not explicitly provided

sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body:
- Add task_type to the save response DTO and populate it from the stored value
- If task_type is intentionally storage-only, document that it won't appear in the response

sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run: `./b4w.ps1 experience list --intent-filter "extract"` when both extract and fill_form entries exist.

sections.label: Expected Behavior

issues.title: Malformed URLs accepted without validation in experience save

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run: `./b4w.ps1 experience save "not-a-valid-url" '{"url":"not-a-valid-url",...}'`

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Either normalize the URL or return a clear error about invalid URL format.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The string "not-a-valid-url" is accepted as-is and used as the domain. No validation or normalization occurs.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: No URL validation is performed on the <url> argument. The input is treated as an opaque string and used directly as the domain key.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add URL validation (protocol check, domain extraction) to the save command
- At minimum, warn if the URL doesn't start with http:// or https://
- Consider normalizing the URL (lowercase hostname, strip fragments) before using as domain

issues.title: Naming inconsistency: 'experience deep learn' (space) vs 'experience deep-learn' (hyphen)

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. Run `./b4w.ps1 help | grep experience` — shows 'experience deep learn'
2. Run `./b4w.ps1 experience deep-learn --help` — works, but help header shows 'experience deep learn'
3. Task documentation and SKILL.md both use 'experience deep-learn'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Consistent naming convention. The help output should match the actual command name. If kebab-case is the convention, it should be 'experience deep-learn' everywhere.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The help output displays 'experience deep learn' (space-separated) while 'experience deep-learn' (hyphenated) also works. The canonical form is ambiguous.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The CLI parser accepts both forms (space and hyphen) but the help text generator uses the space-separated form. The subcommand registration uses 'deep learn' as the canonical name internally.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Standardize on one naming convention (preferably kebab-case: 'experience deep-learn')
- Update the help text generator to output the hyphenated form
- Or accept both but document the canonical form clearly

issues.title: PowerShell wrapper intercepts short flags like -i and -v

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run: `./b4w.ps1 snapshot -i` or `./b4w.ps1 -- snapshot -i`

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The -i flag should be passed to the browser4-cli binary as the interactive snapshot option.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: PowerShell interprets -i as -InformationAction and -v as -Verbose. Even using `--` separator doesn't resolve it for b4w.ps1. The b4w.sh wrapper also fails.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: PowerShell's parameter binder processes short flags before passing them to the wrapped CLI binary. The SKILL.md documents this known issue and suggests workarounds (use b4w.bat or quote arguments), but b4w.bat is not present in the repository and b4w.sh doesn't work in this environment.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Bundle b4w.bat alongside b4w.ps1 for Windows users
- Fix b4w.sh to work properly in Git Bash environments
- Consider using long-form flags (--interactive) as alternatives for commonly intercepted short flags
- Add a note in the SKILL.md that on Git Bash, b4w.sh may not work and users should use pwsh directly
